title: Interferometric braiding of non-Abelian anyons
abstract: The manipulation of non-Abelian anyons is a foundational ingredient for topological quantum computing and underlies topologically protected quantum memories. Here we analyze a quantum-impurity-based protocol for braiding non-Abelian anyons. Exploiting mobile impurities with addressable internal spin states, we provide a concrete protocol to experimentally measure the matrix elements of the $R$ and $F$ matrices that characterize the non-Abelian statistics of anyons. In particular, focusing on the case of Ising and Fibonacci anyons, we illustrate how the anyonic nature of the excitations emerges directly in the Ramsey interferometer we propose. Building on this framework, we further introduce a conventional-to-topological qubit encoder to transfer quantum information from conventional flying qubits into a topologically protected quantum memory.
summary: This paper presents a detailed, experimentally viable protocol using interlayer excitons in TMDs to braid non-Abelian anyons. By measuring interference patterns, the authors demonstrate a method to reconstruct the fundamental R and F matrices that characterize non-Abelian statistics. This work is crucial for realizing topological quantum computation by providing a pathway to encode conventional quantum information into a robust topological memory.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop and demonstrate a concrete, experimental protocol to measure the non-Abelian statistics of anyons and build a hybrid interface for topological quantum memory.
main_result: The proposed interferometric braiding protocol successfully allows for the direct measurement of the R and F matrices characterizing non-Abelian statistics for Ising and Fibonacci anyons.
method: The method involves using mobile impurities (interlayer excitons) whose spin state acts as a conventional qubit, which are braided around non-Abelian anyons within a topologically ordered state.
model_or_system: The physical platform is based on interlayer excitons in Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs) placed near a 2D topologically ordered state hosting the anyons. The protocol utilizes magnetic defects to achieve state-selective transport of the impurities.
key_observables: The key observables are the interference probability patterns, specifically $p_{\uparrow\uparrow}(\phi)$ as a function of the control phase $\phi$ and the number of braiding operations $n$.
important_parameters: The protocol relies on the binding energy $E_b$ and the ability to selectively trap/move impurities based on their spin state using defect potentials.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the ability to prepare specific initial states and relies on the magnetic defect breaking time-reversal symmetry to achieve valley selectivity for impurity transport.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scheme of the hybrid interface (photonic to topological qubit), the setup for braiding multiple Ising anyons, and the resulting probability patterns $p_{\uparrow\uparrow}(\phi)$ for both Ising and Fibonacci anyons.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general concept of using impurities for braiding, details the specific protocol steps (pulse sequence, movement), and then applies this to reconstruct the R and F matrices for Ising and Fibonacci anyons, concluding with the qubit encoding scheme.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly tangible, solid-state platform (TMDs) for realizing and characterizing fundamental topological quantum phenomena, bridging abstract topological theory with solid-state experimental feasibility.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Scheme of the proposed hybrid interface between the flying photonic qubit and the topological qubit. The topolog- ical qubit consists of excitations (represented as red vortices) on top of a 2D topologically ordered (TO) state. In a first step, the flying photonic qubit is used to initialize the spin qubit, encoded in the (pseudo-)spin state of the impurity. In a second step, the state of the spin qubit is encoded into the topological qubit using the braiding protocol detailed in the main text.

FIG. 2. Top-down view of four Ising anyons of type σ. The dashed blue (purple) lines represent the braiding of anyons σ2 (σ1) and σ3 (σ2). This operation corresponds to the braiding operator ˆB23 ( ˆB12).

FIG. 3. Probabilities of finding both impurities in the ↑state when the topological system is initialized in the state |0⟩top for Ising anyons. The probability pattern goes to zero for n = 0, 2 braiding operations (see blue and orange curves), while it is always nonzero for n = 1, 3 braiding operations (see red and purple dashed curves) — demonstrating the non- Abelian character of the anyons.

FIG. 4. (a) Top-down view of three Fibonacci anyons of type τ. The dashed blue (purple) lines represent the braiding of anyons τ2 (τ1) and τ3 (τ2). This operation corresponds to the braiding operator ˆB23 ( ˆB12). (b) Probabilities of finding both impurities in the ↑state when the topological system is initialized in the state |0⟩top for Fibonacci anyons. The probability pattern goes to zero for n = 0 braiding operations (blue curve), while it is always nonzero for n = 1 braiding operations (orange curve) — demonstrating the non-Abelian character of the anyons.
